      "observations": [
        "The full379-line six-file patch implements outgoing EWS password lookup with an ews://host login origin/realm that excludes the service port. It propagates login service/FindLogins/password errors, removes null options, filters matching usernames and uses the first matching login. A failed GetUsername skips that candidate; no match returns an empty string. This mostly copies the incoming lookup contract, but the exact error behavior differs from the incoming loop that propagates GetUsername failure. It does not add a password prompt.",
        "AuthenticationProvider::password changes from nsCString to nsString, matching the incoming password API and avoiding an intermediate UTF-16/UTF-8 conversion. get_credentials converts the final values into Rust Strings for the historical Credentials::Basic encoder. The outgoing send path obtains those credentials before constructing the EWS client. These exact type boundaries do not establish a universal string encoding convention.",
        "The new test stores one ASCII username/password at a port-free login URI, sends a5-line fixture, awaits listener completion and checks the two-part Basic header/base64 value. The historical fake server only records the header and returns a static successful CreateItem response; it does not validate the credentials. Non-ASCII, multiple-login selection, missing credentials and lookup failure paths are not asserted by this added test. Fixed tests later move to exchange and the fake validates credentials; fixed shared authentication delegates Basic/NTLM to Necko and password lookup to the password module. That architecture is already covered by the reused lesson, not credited as this landing.",
        "Reviewer explicitly requests FindLogins failure propagation; author applies it, accepts the optional empty-options wording and adds the test before reacceptance. Native C-string availability/MSRV explanation is the author’s historical report, not a current version claim. Try links/build statuses are retained without a passing runtime claim."
